items.text: The Army will blow up nearly five tons of unstable explosive in Iowa on Wednesday morning, it said, after a federal appeals court cleared the plan Monday night.
items.detail: A three-judge 8th Circuit panel denied the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club's emergency request to keep the EPA's permit on hold, saying the groups were unlikely to win and that the degraded lead azide risks "an uncontrolled and unplanned explosion" without the permit's safeguards; the underlying challenge continues. Earlier Monday, President Trump said the detonation of 68 drums at the Middletown plant would wait for the court and be "fully subject" to Gov.-elect Rob Sand agreeing. Sand did not say yes or no, saying the administration "should make this decision" on the information from its own experts and urging it to share that information with the public. Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said every agency involved agreed the Army should proceed with a "carefully controlled detonation" Wednesday morning, and the Army said Gov. Kim Reynolds supports it.
items.why: The blast could spread lead dust over farms and towns in Iowa and Illinois, and the Army says waiting risks a bigger, uncontrolled explosion as temperatures fall.

items.text: New U.S. strikes on Iran may come after the New Year if talks fail, President Trump told Fox News; Iran's top negotiator said Tuesday it will not talk until its conditions are met.
items.detail: In comments to Fox News on Sunday, Trump said he is inclined to order strikes after the new year without a deal, called Iran's negotiators "professional tap dancers" and said Iran is "more aggressive now than before the election." He dared Iran to challenge the U.S. naval blockade of its ports. On Tuesday, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's lead negotiator, told parliament Iran will not negotiate with the United States until its "seven conditions" are met, state-affiliated Mehr News Agency reported. Iran has demanded an end to the blockade, sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets before formal talks.
items.why: It sets a rough timeline for a possible return to full-scale war as indirect talks through Qatar stall.

items.text: Rep. Ilhan Omar could claim the privacy protections of a sitting member of Congress during the federal search of her home, unsealed court records show.
items.detail: Magistrate Judge Matthew Sharbaugh, who approved the Oct. 12 search of the Minnesota Democrat's Washington home, rejected the Justice Department's view that the Speech or Debate Clause privilege covers only official offices and some devices; the government agreed to a protocol letting Omar assert the privilege before agents searched. Chief Judge James Boasberg ordered the partial unsealing after more than a dozen news organizations sued, but kept the 67-page search warrant affidavit sealed. The heavily redacted filings shed no new light on why the search happened or what it found. Omar has not been charged and denies wrongdoing; the AP has reported investigators are examining her family's immigration paperwork.
items.why: It is the first public look at how a court weighed the rare search of a sitting member of Congress's home weeks before an election.

items.text: A car bomb outside the Meta state governor's office in Villavicencio, Colombia, wounded 21 people Monday night, local health officials said.
items.detail: Meta's health department said 21 people were hurt, including five security guards at the building; police reported no deaths. The blast heavily damaged the government building on the city's central park and nearby buildings. President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism" and said his government will not negotiate with armed groups; no group has claimed the attack.
items.why: It is one of the most serious urban bombings in Colombia since the new government vowed to crush armed groups.

items.text: An explosion at a crowded hot pot restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam, killed six people and injured more than a dozen Tuesday morning, local time.
items.detail: Police said preliminary findings point to a gas explosion that brought down part of the building; more than 14 people were hospitalized, one with a traumatic brain injury, and rescuers searched the rubble for anyone trapped. Nearby houses were damaged and residents of unsafe buildings were moved.
items.why: It is one of the deadliest accidental blasts in Vietnam's capital in years.

items.text: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's CEO and president Monday, effective immediately, less than two weeks after he resigned; the company's shares jumped about 31%.
items.detail: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring Huang back, and to his board seat, after meetings in which it said it was satisfied with his "candor and ability to lead." The board said it received input from "senior levels of the United States government" and is confident his return "poses no national security risk." Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials suspected of working for Chinese intelligence; board chair Harvey Jones said on the Nov. 17 earnings call that the board did not intend to reinstate him. President Trump called it "the correct and proper decision" on Truth Social and said the attorney general has no evidence Huang broke the law. Colette Kress, interim CEO since Nov. 12, returns to her finance role. Nvidia closed up about 31.5%, its best day since 2000, adding roughly $900 billion in market value.
items.why: The return of the head of the world's most valuable chipmaker, with the government's blessing, reset the AI trade that dragged stocks into a correction last week.

items.text: The S&P 500 jumped 4.7% Monday, its best day since April 2025, as Huang's return to Nvidia ended a seven-day slide in U.S. stocks.
items.detail: The S&P 500 closed at 7,237.17, the Nasdaq Composite rose 6.5% to 24,089.56 and the Dow gained about 1,448 points, or 3%, to 49,595.31, recovering more than half of last week's plunge that pushed the S&P and Dow into a correction. Chip stocks led: the Philadelphia semiconductor index rose 14%, with Micron up 19% and TSMC up 15%. Nasdaq 100 futures rose so fast before the open that a rare circuit breaker was triggered, Bloomberg reported. The VIX fear gauge fell about 25%. Separately, New York Fed President John Williams said Monday the Fed has "work to do" on inflation and must act "over time" to reach its 2% goal; markets fully price a quarter-point rate increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting.
items.why: Last week's AI rout hit retirement accounts across the country; Monday clawed back much of it ahead of Wednesday's PCE inflation report.

items.text: The Army's planned detonation of nearly five tons of unstable explosive in Iowa is on hold after President Trump ordered it paused Monday until a court allows it.
items.detail: Trump said the military will not blow up the 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown until the 8th Circuit lets it proceed, and made it "fully subject" to Iowa Governor-elect Rob Sand agreeing. He said a controlled blast would be safer and that he would hold Sand responsible for any harm if the material is not destroyed. The Army had planned the detonation for Wednesday despite the court's pause of the EPA emergency permit, and the Justice Department asked judges Sunday to lift that pause. Environmental groups sued over health and pollution risks to nearby residents.
items.why: It removes, for now, the threat of a blast that neighbors feared would spread lead over their homes.

items.text: NATO is sending an AWACS early-warning aircraft to Poland after three Russian cruise missiles crashed there Friday, alliance and Polish officials said Monday.
items.detail: Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski announced the deployment after an emergency North Atlantic Council meeting in Brussels; a NATO spokesperson said the alliance's top commander, Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, authorized it and is examining additional assets. Poland asked allies for stronger air defenses on the eastern flank but did not invoke Article 4. Polish prosecutors say all three objects were Kh-101 missiles; Zalewski called the incursion an "obvious provocation."
items.why: It is NATO's first concrete military response to Russian missiles landing on alliance soil.

items.text: Grok, Elon Musk's AI chatbot, let users make sexualized images of real people, including children, without consent, Virginia and Oregon charged in lawsuits Monday.
items.detail: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones sued SpaceX, which now runs X and xAI, saying the companies failed to stop Grok from generating non-consensual intimate images and child sexual abuse material while promoting the platform as safe; Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a separate, similar suit. The states seek penalties and new consumer protections. Virginia says Grok could fabricate sexual images from a single existing photo.
items.why: It is the first state legal action over AI-made sexual deepfakes on one of the biggest social platforms.

also.text: Welgemda, a twice-daily oral drug, is the first FDA-approved treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, the agency said Monday.
also.detail: The FDA approved Welgemda (ribitol) for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, an inherited muscle-wasting disease caused by FKRP gene mutations, for adults and children weighing at least 30 kg. In a 112-patient placebo-controlled trial, patients on the drug improved in walking speed and lung function after 12 months. Common side effects were diarrhea, stomach pain and joint pain. It is made by ML Bio Solutions and distributed by BridgeBio Pharma.
also.why: Patients with this progressive disease, which can take away walking and breathing, had no approved treatment.

week.text: Giredestrant, a daily pill from Genentech, was approved by the FDA Monday to help keep common early-stage breast cancer from coming back after surgery.
week.detail: The FDA approved giredestrant (Wilserdly), an oral estrogen-receptor blocker, as a single agent for adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative Stage I to III breast cancer at intermediate to high risk of recurrence. ER-positive, HER2-negative tumors are the most common type of breast cancer; Genentech calls it the first new hormone therapy for this setting in over 20 years.
week.why: Hundreds of thousands of women take years of hormone pills after breast cancer surgery; this adds a new option.

week.text: Virginia's law banning masks for ICE officers stays blocked, a federal appeals court ruled Monday, but the state may limit local police cooperation with immigration agents.
week.detail: A 4th Circuit panel upheld Judge Robert Payne's order blocking Virginia from enforcing its law requiring federal immigration officers to show their faces and identify themselves, finding the state cannot directly regulate federal agents. But it vacated his block on a second law restricting localities' 287(g) agreements with ICE, saying states need not help with federal enforcement. Judge Toby Heytens wrote the opinion, joined by Judge DeAndrea Benjamin; Judge Robert King concurred in part and dissented in part. A federal judge blocked Connecticut's similar mask law on Nov. 20.
week.why: It sets the rules in five states for how far states can go in curbing ICE tactics as more pass mask bans.
week.source: U.S. Court of Appeals for the 4th Circuit

week.text: Social media companies cannot be held liable for the 2022 Buffalo supermarket massacre, New York's highest court ruled Monday, 4-3.
week.detail: The Court of Appeals upheld dismissal of suits by survivors and victims' families against YouTube, Reddit, Twitch, Discord, 4chan and others, which argued the platforms radicalized the white supremacist gunman who killed 10 Black people at a Tops market. The majority said the shooter's conduct was so extraordinary that it was not a foreseeable result of the platforms' design, so the companies were not the legal cause of the injuries.
week.why: It is a major test of whether tech platforms can be sued for violence linked to what users see on them.

upcoming.detail: Release date per the Conference Board. The index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, up from 84.2 in September.
